Q3510872.title: Bola Tinubu
Q3510872.wikitext:
{{people-cleanup}} [[File:Bola Tinubu portrait.jpg|thumb|With full confidence in our ability, I declare that these things are within our proximate reach because my name is Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and I am the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.]] [[w:Chieftain|Chief]] '''[[w:Bola Tinubu|Bola Ahmed Adekunle Tinubu]]''', [[w:Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic|GCFR]], (born 29 March 1952) is a [[Nigerian]] [[politician]] who is the 16th and current president of [[Federal Republic of Nigeria]]. He was the governor of Lagos State from 1999 to 2007; and senator for Lagos West in the Third Republic. {{political-stub}} {{center|'''Whether you voted for me during the elections, or not, I am your President.''' [[#Taglines|Taglines]]}} == Quotes == ===1990s === ====1999==== *As flag-bearers, we are not unmindful of the heavy burden and responsibility that we carry. We are not unmindful of the huge expectations of our people, young and old, man and woman, able and disabled. Nor are we unmindful of the misery and poverty that the generality of our people have had to endure almost forty years after Independence. **''Inaugural speech as Governor of Lagos State.''(May 1999) === 2010s === ==== 2010 ==== There is no way the Independent Electoral Commission led by Prof. Attahiru Jega can give the nation a credible Election next year. *''[https://archivi.ng/search/_1TtFIwBg5yxONaM-hDG?from=extract=Bola%2Bahmed%2Btinubu%26page=5%26sort_by=relevance PM News Interview].''(June 2010) ===2020s=== ====2020==== *The Corona crisis will shrink the inflow of dollars. Hopefully, this is temporary, no more than a few months. CBN can allow some downward pressure on the naira without energetically intervening to defend the exchange rate. Only if and when the rate seems that it might dip precipitously should the CBN intervene. **[https://www.thisdaylive.com/index.php/2020/03/29/covid-19-tinubu-advises-fg-to-increase-naira-expenditure/ Adresses Federal Government on COVID-19:](April 2020) *Those who suffered casualties during the gunshot need to answer some questions too. How are they there? How long where they there? What kind of characters are they? Even-though we want to help we still must extract information to help the government prepare in future or understand how and when to react. **Speaking to the Press on [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vnO4blAQm-Y&ab_channel=ChannelsTelevision ENDSARs shooting] ===2022 Presidential Campaign === *The other candidates are all good men. But I sincerely believe I am the person this moment calls for. *I humbly ask that you nominate me as the party’s presidential candidate. Together we shall forge an even better party and a greater Nigeria. *I have the experience. I led the transformation of Lagos from a dangerous, unwelcoming place in 1999 to a clean, safe, and vibrant place and the 5th largest economy in all of Africa. I am a serious man with a serious purpose and I will use all that I know and all of my abilities to the benefit of the people. ** {{citation | url = https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2022/06/08/i-am-the-man-of-the-moment-tinubu/ | title = '''Full text of the abridged speech read by Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the APC Convention on Tuesday night''' | periodical = Daily Post | date = 2022-05-08 | }} ====2023==== *Over six decades ago, our founding fathers gave bravely of themselves to place Nigeria on the map as an independent nation. **[https://guardian.ng/features/for-the-record/full-text-of-president-bola-tinubus-inauguration-speech/ Inaugural Speech as President] *The peaceful transition from one government to another is now our political tradition. This handover symbolizes our trust in God, our enduring faith in representative governance and our belief in our ability to reshape this nation into the society it was always meant to be. **[https://guardian.ng/features/for-the-record/full-text-of-president-bola-tinubus-inauguration-speech/ Inaugural Speech as President] *We must promote unity and stability for all. Whether you voted for me during the elections, or not, I am your President. I will work on your behalf to ensure a turning point of prosperity. ** {{citation | url = https://dailypost.ng/2023/06/24/details-of-tinubus-meeting-with-david-alaba-oga-other-nigerians-in-diaspora/ | title = Details of Tinubu’s meeting with David Alaba, Oga, other Nigerians in diaspora | periodical = Daily Post | date = 2023-05-24 | accessdate = 2023-05-25 }} ====2024==== * The hallmark of a leader is to do what must be done when it should be done. ** [https://thesun.ng/10-notable-quotes-from-president-tinubus-first-media-chat/ Bola Tinubu speaking on the hallmark of a leader] == 2023 Quotes == === Presidential Ignuaral Address === * I stand before you honoured to assume the sacred mandate you have given me. My love for this nation is abiding. My confidence in its people, unwavering. And my faith in God Almighty, absolute. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.At the beginning of his inaugural address after taking the oath of office as President of Nigeria, Tinubu expressed gratitude to Nigerians, affirmed his confidence in the nation, and pledged to serve with faith and commitment. * As a nation, we have long ago decided to march beyond the dimness of night into the open day of renewed national hope. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Tinubu described Nigeria as a country moving toward a brighter future, urging citizens to embrace hope and national renewal. * We are too great a nation and too grounded as a people to rob ourselves of our finest destiny.. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Encouraging Nigerians to believe in their collective potential, Tinubu argued that the country possessed the strength and resilience needed to achieve lasting progress. * To those who voted otherwise, I extend my hand across the political divide. I ask you to grasp it in national affinity and brotherhood. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Following a closely contested presidential election, Tinubu appealed for reconciliation and national unity, inviting all Nigerians to work together regardless of political affiliation. * For me, political coloration has faded away. All I see are Nigerians. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Tinubu emphasized that, as President, he intended to govern all Nigerians impartially rather than along party or political lines. * We shall not allow events of the recent past to divert us from our steadfast resolve to make Nigeria a better place for all. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Tinubu urged Nigerians to move beyond the tensions surrounding the 2023 general election and remain committed to national progress and reconciliation. * Our destiny as a people is to be one united nation, and this is the path we shall pursue. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.The President reaffirmed his commitment to national unity, stressing that his administration would work to strengthen cohesion across Nigeria's diverse communities. *Fuel subsidy is gone. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.In one of the most memorable moments of the inaugural address, Tinubu announced the end of the fuel subsidy regime, describing it as a necessary economic reform to redirect national resources toward development. * Budgetary spending that is not backed by actual revenue has for too long fuelled the evil of inflation. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.While outlining his administration's economic priorities, Tinubu argued for fiscal discipline and responsible public spending to address inflation and promote macroeconomic stability. * Our administration shall target a higher GDP growth and significantly reduce unemployment. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Presenting his economic vision, Tinubu pledged to pursue policies aimed at accelerating economic growth, creating jobs, and improving the living standards of Nigerians. * Our government shall review all complaints about multiple taxation and various anti-investment inhibitions. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.While outlining his economic agenda, President Tinubu pledged to improve Nigeria's business environment by addressing excessive taxation and regulatory barriers that discourage investment.
* Security shall be the top priority of our administration because neither prosperity nor justice can prevail amidst insecurity and violence. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Tinubu identified national security as the foundation for economic growth, justice, and social stability, promising to strengthen Nigeria's security architecture. * We shall invest more in our people, especially our youth. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.The President emphasized that developing human capital, particularly through opportunities for young Nigerians, would be a central objective of his administration.The President emphasized that developing human capital, particularly through opportunities for young Nigerians, would be a central objective of his administration. * Education shall be given the highest priority because it is the greatest weapon against poverty. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.While discussing social development, Tinubu stressed the importance of education as a tool for reducing poverty and expanding opportunities for Nigerians. * I will be a fair leader to all Nigerians. ** https://www.channelstv.com/2023/05/29/full-text-of-president-tinubus-inaugural-speech/.Near the conclusion of his inaugural address, Tinubu reaffirmed his commitment to govern without discrimination and to serve every Nigerian regardless of political affiliation, ethnicity, or religion. *
Nigeria will be impartially governed according to the constitution and the rule of law. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.While outlining the principles that would guide his administration, President Tinubu pledged that his government would be anchored on constitutional governance and the rule of law. * We shall defend the nation from terror and all forms of criminality that threaten the peace and stability of our country and our subregion. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.In setting out his administration's priorities, Tinubu committed to strengthening national security and combating terrorism and other forms of violent crime. * We shall remodel our economy to bring about growth and development through job creation, food security and an end of extreme poverty. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Presenting his economic agenda, Tinubu identified economic growth, employment, food security and poverty reduction as central objectives of his administration. * In our administration, women and youth will feature prominently. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.While listing the guiding principles of his government, Tinubu pledged that women and young people would play significant roles in his administration. * Our government will continue to take proactive steps such as championing a credit culture to discourage corruption while strengthening the effectiveness and efficiency of the various anti-corruption agencies. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu outlined his anti-corruption approach, stating that his administration would strengthen institutions while promoting financial practices that discourage corruption. * Our constitution and laws give us a nation on paper. We must work harder at bringing these noble documents to life by strengthening the bonds of economic collaboration, social cohesion, and cultural understanding. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.President Tinubu called on Nigerians to move beyond constitutional ideals by building stronger economic, social and cultural ties to create a more united nation. * Our national currency shall be treated with respect by all. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.While outlining financial reforms, Tinubu pledged that his administration would restore confidence in the naira and strengthen the integrity of Nigeria's monetary system. * Interest rates need to be reduced to increase investment and consumer purchasing in ways that sustain the economy at a higher level. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Discussing economic policy, Tinubu argued that lower interest rates would encourage investment, boost consumer spending and support long-term economic growth. * We shall require the banks to increase lending to the economy and avoid multiple and excessive charges on customers. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Presenting his economic programme, Tinubu said his administration would work with the banking sector to expand access to credit while protecting customers from excessive banking charges. * This is the proudest day of my life. But this day does not belong to me. It belongs to you, the people of Nigeria. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/. In the closing section of his inaugural address, Tinubu dedicated the significance of his inauguration to the Nigerian people, emphasizing that the presidency is a public trust. * Our burdens may make us bend at times, but they shall never break us. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Reflecting on Nigeria's history, President Tinubu praised the resilience of Nigerians, arguing that despite hardship, the nation had remained united and hopeful. * .We are here to further mend and heal this nation, not tear and injure it. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu appealed for national healing after the 2023 general election, emphasizing reconciliation over division. * They have taken their concerns to court. Seeking legal redress is their right and I fully defend their exercise of this right. This is the essence of the rule of law. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Addressing the presidential election disputes, Tinubu acknowledged the right of his opponents to challenge the results in court and described judicial review as a fundamental element of the rule of law. * We must never allow the labor of those who came before us to wither in vain but to blossom and bring forth a better reality. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Honouring Nigeria's founding generation, Tinubu urged citizens to build upon the sacrifices of those who secured the country's independence and democracy. * As we contain threats to peace, we shall also retool our foreign policy to more actively lead the regional and continental quest for collective prosperity. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.While outlining his foreign policy priorities, Tinubu said Nigeria would take a more active leadership role in promoting peace and shared prosperity across West Africa and the African continent. * Today, Fate and Destiny join together to place the torch of human progress in our very hands. We dare not let it slip. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.President Tinubu urged Nigerians to seize the opportunity to build a better nation, describing the moment as a historic responsibility entrusted to the present generation. * We lift high this torch so that it might shine on every household and in every heart that calls itself Nigerian. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Using the metaphor of a torch, Tinubu spoke of hope, unity and shared national purpose, calling on Nigerians to work together for the country's future. * Our administration shall govern on your behalf but never rule over you. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu assured Nigerians that his government would be based on democratic accountability and public service rather than authoritarian rule. * We shall consult and dialogue but never dictate. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Continuing his democratic vision, Tinubu pledged that his administration would engage citizens and stakeholders through consultation instead of imposing decisions unilaterally. * We shall reach out to all but never put down a single person for holding views contrary to our own. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.The President promised an inclusive style of governance that respected differing opinions while encouraging national dialogue and mutual respect. * The outcome reflected the will of the people. However, my victory does not render me any more Nigerian than my opponents. Nor does it render them any less patriotic. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Addressing the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu acknowledged his political opponents and emphasized that electoral victory did not diminish their patriotism or citizenship. * They shall forever be my fellow compatriots. And I will treat them as such. They represent important constituencies and concerns that wisdom dare not ignore. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Continuing his remarks on post-election reconciliation, Tinubu pledged to respect his political opponents and recognize the legitimacy of the constituencies they represent. * Our mission is to improve our way of life in a manner that nurtures our humanity, encourages compassion toward one another, and duly rewards our collective effort to resolve the social ills that seek to divide us. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.While explaining what he called the "Nigerian ideal," Tinubu said that national progress should be measured not only by economic indicators but also by compassion, unity and shared responsibility. * The South must not only seek good for itself but must understand that its interests are served when good comes to the North. The North must see the South likewise. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu called for mutual understanding and national solidarity, arguing that Nigeria's regions are interdependent and prosper best when they pursue each other's well-being. * Whether from the winding creeks of the Niger Delta, the vastness of the northern savannah, the boardrooms of Lagos, the bustling capital of Abuja, or the busy markets of Onitsha, you are all my people. As your President, I shall serve with prejudice toward none but compassion and amity towards all. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Emphasizing inclusive governance, Tinubu affirmed that every Nigerian, regardless of region or background, would receive equal consideration under his administration. * As citizens, we declare as one unified people devoted to one unified national cause, that as long as this world exists, Nigeria shall exist. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Reflecting on Nigeria's resilience, President Tinubu declared that despite years of predictions about the country's collapse, Nigerians remained united and committed to preserving the nation. * The peaceful transition from one government to another is now our political tradition. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu described the transfer of power as evidence of Nigeria's democratic maturity and enduring commitment to representative government. * We have endured hardships that would have made other societies crumble. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.The President praised the resilience of Nigerians, noting that the country had survived significant challenges through collective perseverance. * This nation’s journey has been shaped by the prayers of millions, and the collective sacrifices of us all. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.Tinubu acknowledged the contributions of ordinary Nigerians, saying the country's progress had been built on the prayers and sacrifices of its people. * On this day, Nigeria affirms its rightful place among the world's great democracies. There, Nigeria shall reside forever. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/inaugural-address-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu-delivered-on-29-may-2023/.In the concluding section of his inaugural address, Tinubu expressed confidence in Nigeria's democratic future and its place among the world's established democracies. == Quotes== Democracy Day National Broadcast. 12 June, 2023. * It is exactly three decades today that Nigerians went to the polls to exercise their inalienable right to elect a President of their choice to lead the transition from military dictatorship to a representative government of the people. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Opening his first Democracy Day national broadcast as President, Tinubu reflected on the significance of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and its place in Nigeria's democratic history. * The abortion, by military fiat, of the decisive victory of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola... turned out, ironically, to be the seed that germinated into the prolonged struggle that gave birth to the democracy we currently enjoy since 1999. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Tinubu described the annulment of the June 12, 1993 election as the catalyst that eventually led to Nigeria's return to democratic rule. * The fierce opposition to the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and the unrelenting pro-democracy onslaught it unleashed was the equivalent of the battle against colonial rule by our founding fathers that resulted in the gaining of Nigeria's independence in 1960. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.The President compared the struggle to restore the June 12 mandate with Nigeria's independence movement, describing both as defining moments in the nation's history. * Without the historic struggle of the June 12 movement, there would have been no foundation for the democracy that we enjoy today. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Tinubu credited the sacrifices of pro-democracy activists with laying the groundwork for Nigeria's current democratic system. * As we mark this year's Democracy Day, let us rededicate ourselves to the ideals of democratic governance. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Concluding the historical reflection, Tinubu urged Nigerians to renew their commitment to democracy and its core principles. * But the beauty of democracy is that those who win today can lose tomorrow and those who lose today will have an opportunity to compete and win in the next round of elections. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.President Tinubu emphasized that democracy guarantees periodic elections and peaceful changes in leadership, ensuring that electoral defeat is never permanent. * Those who cannot endure and accept the pain of defeat in elections do not deserve the joy of victory when it is their turn to triumph. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.While discussing democratic values, Tinubu urged political actors to accept electoral outcomes and uphold democratic principles regardless of whether they win or lose. * Those who disagree with the outcome of the elections are taking full advantage of the constitutional provisions to seek redress in court and that is one of the reasons why democracy is still the best form of government invented by man. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.The President defended the constitutional right of aggrieved candidates to challenge election results through the courts, describing judicial review as a strength of democracy. * For Chief MKO Abiola, the symbol of this day, in whose memory June 12 became a national holiday, democracy is eternal. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Tinubu paid tribute to Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola, presenting him as the enduring symbol of Nigeria's democratic struggle. * It is about rule of law and vibrant judiciary that can be trusted to deliver justice and strengthen institutions. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Describing the foundations of democracy, Tinubu stressed the importance of the rule of law, an independent judiciary, and strong institutions. * We must never take this democracy for granted. We must forever jealously guard and protect it like a precious jewel. For, a people can never truly appreciate the freedoms and rights democracy guarantees them until they lose it. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.President Tinubu urged Nigerians to cherish and protect democratic governance, warning that its value is often fully appreciated only after it is lost. * True, rancorous debates, interminable wrangling, ceaseless quarrels, bitter electoral contestations may be perceived by some as unattractive features of democracy. But they also testify to its merit and value. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.While acknowledging the imperfections of democratic politics, Tinubu argued that open disagreement is evidence of a healthy democratic system rather than a weakness. * The democracy that will yield right dividends to the people who are the shareholders means more than just freedom of choice and right to get people into elective offices. It means social and economic justice for our people. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Tinubu argued that democracy should deliver tangible improvements in the lives of citizens, not merely periodic elections. * There is nothing divine about poverty. It is a man-made problem that can be eliminated with clearly thought out social and economic policies. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Referring to Chief M. K. O. Abiola's *Farewell to Poverty* campaign manifesto, Tinubu echoed the belief that poverty is not inevitable but can be overcome through sound public policy. * I feel your pain. This is one decision we must bear to save our country from going under and take our resources away from the stranglehold of a few unpatriotic elements. ** https://fmino.gov.ng/text-of-democracy-day-national-broadcast-by-president-bola-ahmed-tinubu/.Speaking about the removal of fuel subsidy, Tinubu acknowledged the hardship Nigerians would face while defending the decision as necessary for the country's long-term survival. * == Quotes== === Democracy Day National Broadcast, June 2024 === * On this day, 31 years ago, we entered our rites of passage to becoming a true and enduring democratic society. * https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Opening his 2024 Democracy Day broadcast, President Tinubu reflected on the beginning of Nigeria's democratic journey following the June 12, 1993 election. * Going through this passage was hard and dangerous. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Tinubu acknowledged the sacrifices and difficulties encountered during Nigeria's struggle to restore democratic rule. * We lost great heroes and heroines along the way. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.The President paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the struggle for democracy, including Chief M. K. O. Abiola, Kudirat Abiola, General Shehu Musa Yar'Adua and Pa Alfred Rewane. * Our democracy is more than a historic fact. It is a living, breathing reality. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Tinubu described democracy as an active system that must continue to be nurtured rather than merely remembered as a historical achievement. * We must continue to cherish, nurture and deepen it. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.The President urged Nigerians to strengthen democratic institutions and preserve the country's democratic gains. * During the fateful six years that followed, we fought and struggled for our natural rights as human beings put on this earth by the divine hand of our Creator. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.President Tinubu reflected on the years following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 election, describing the pro-democracy struggle that eventually restored civilian rule. * The power of an idea, the power of the people proved more potent than all the guns and munitions, and the threats of the strongmen. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Reflecting on Nigeria's struggle against military rule, Tinubu said that the determination of the people ultimately prevailed over authoritarian power. * Democracy is a way of life that encompasses a broad outlook of which elections are but a part. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Explaining his understanding of democracy, Tinubu argued that democracy extends beyond periodic elections to a broader system of governance and civic life. * What democracy demands is that we do not resolve differences through force and repression. But we make allowance for the legitimacy of views that differ from our own. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Tinubu emphasized that democratic societies resolve disagreements peacefully and respect differing opinions rather than suppressing them. * Democracy is neither a foreign nor abstract concept devoid of meaning for us. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Tinubu rejected the notion that democracy is alien to Nigeria, arguing that it is a meaningful system rooted in the country's political aspirations. * It is the primary way we govern ourselves and the manner by which we become the architects of our individual and collective destinies. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Continuing his explanation of democracy, Tinubu described it as the system through which Nigerians shape both their personal futures and the nation's future. * The real test of a functioning democracy is not whether people agree all the time but whether they can disagree without undermining the fabric of the society. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Tinubu argued that peaceful disagreement, rather than uniformity of opinion, is one of the defining characteristics of a healthy democracy. * We must be vigilant in expanding and defending the liberties our democracy provides. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.The President urged Nigerians to protect democratic freedoms and continue strengthening democratic institutions. * We must continue the work of building a more just, prosperous and united nation. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-national-broadcast-on-the-25th-anniversary-of-unbroken-democracy-in-nigeria-democracy-day-12th-june-2024/.Towards the close of the address, Tinubu called on Nigerians to continue working together to strengthen justice, prosperity and national unity. * With profound honour, I stand before this joint session of our National Assembly; a parliament that embodies the will of the Nigerian people. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu opened his Democracy Day address by recognizing the National Assembly as the democratic institution representing the collective will of Nigerians. * Today, as I entered this grand edifice built from the sweat and toil of our democratic yearning, my heart stirred. It was a blend of accomplishment and resolve. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Reflecting on his arrival at the National Assembly for the 2025 Democracy Day commemoration, President Tinubu expressed both satisfaction with Nigeria's democratic progress and determination to continue strengthening the nation's democratic institutions. * Since 1999, democracy has risen from the ashes and destitution of military rule to take its rightful place as the only mode of governance of our resilient and beloved people. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu reflected on Nigeria's democratic journey since the return to civilian rule in 1999, describing democracy as the country's accepted system of government after years of military rule. * With every footstep I took through these hallowed halls up to the moment I now stand before you, I remembered that we still have much further to go. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/..While addressing the National Assembly, Tinubu acknowledged Nigeria's democratic achievements but emphasized that the country's democratic development remains an ongoing journey. * I hereby affirm before our Merciful and Almighty God and all men my resolve to do all that I can to safeguard and build our democracy as the Divine hand intends for us to do. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu reaffirmed his commitment to protecting and strengthening Nigeria's democracy, pledging before the nation and God to uphold democratic governance. * Since 2018, we have celebrated Democracy Day on this day; to commemorate the sacrifices of the men and women who fought to restore democratic governance to Nigeria. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu reflected on the significance of June 12 as Democracy Day, noting that it commemorates those who struggled to restore democratic rule in Nigeria.
* Let me pay tribute to former President Muhammadu Buhari for reaching back into history to rectify a national misdeed by making June 12 Democracy Day and by officially acknowledging Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola and his running mate, Babagana Kingibe, as the victors and thus duly elected President and Vice President respectively of Nigeria after the June 12, 1993 elections. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu commended former President Muhammadu Buhari for officially recognizing the outcome of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and declaring June 12 as Nigeria's Democracy Day.
* Year by year, election after election, every time we debate instead of battle, discuss instead of fight, and argue instead of destroy, we preserve the institutions of democracy. More importantly, we weave the culture of democracy into the very fabric of our nation. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu emphasized that peaceful political engagement and constructive disagreement strengthen democratic institutions and deepen democratic culture.
* Whilst Chief MKO Abiola is June 12's central figure, we must not forget the long list of those who equally deserve to be called heroes of Nigerian democracy. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.The President acknowledged that, alongside Chief M. K. O. Abiola, many others made significant sacrifices in Nigeria's struggle for democratic governance.
* We must celebrate the courage of Alhaja Kudirat Abiola and Pa Alfred Rewane, both of whom were murdered by agents of military repression. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu paid tribute to Kudirat Abiola and Alfred Rewane, recognizing their sacrifices during Nigeria's pro-democracy struggle.
* We also remember the many civil rights activists, journalists, and politicians imprisoned, exiled, tossed aside, tortured and beaten by the military regime. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.After paying tribute to Kudirat Abiola and Alfred Rewane, President Tinubu honoured the many pro-democracy activists who suffered persecution during military rule.
* We must celebrate and remember the contributions of all those who played significant roles in Nigeria's democratic evolution. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu called on Nigerians to honour the individuals whose sacrifices and efforts contributed to the country's democratic development.
* Our nation is not perfect, but it is strong. Our democracy is not invincible, but it is alive. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu reflected on the resilience of Nigeria and its democratic institutions, acknowledging both their challenges and enduring strength. == Qoutes == === 2025 Democracy Day Address to the Joint Session of the National Assembly=== * The struggle was never the province of any one group or section of the country, it was pan-Nigerian in its conception and will be even more pan-Nigerian as we strive to perfect it. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu emphasized that the struggle for democracy was a national movement involving Nigerians from every part of the country, and he urged continued collective effort to strengthen democratic governance. * It is fitting that I come to this chamber. You are the authors of the people's law, and I must be their faithful implementer. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Addressing members of the National Assembly, Tinubu acknowledged the legislature's constitutional role in making laws while affirming his responsibility to faithfully implement them. * While we may not always agree, we must forge a way to work together because this is what democracy demands of us. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.The President called for cooperation between the executive and legislative branches despite differences in opinion, describing collaboration as an essential requirement of democracy. * I pledge myself to this cooperation and ask that you do the same for the good of our people. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu concluded his appeal to the National Assembly by pledging cooperation and urging lawmakers to work together with the executive in the interest of Nigerians. * In 2006, the 5th National Assembly protected our democracy against an unseemly third-term bid that would have ripped our Constitution apart. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu cited the National Assembly's rejection of the proposed third-term agenda in 2006 as a defining moment in the defence of Nigeria's constitutional democracy. * In 2010, the National Assembly, through the doctrine of necessity, opened the door for then-Vice President Goodluck Jonathan to become the Acting President following the illness of his predecessor. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu highlighted the National Assembly's invocation of the doctrine of necessity in 2010 as an example of protecting constitutional governance during a national crisis. * Even under the military, the National Assembly tried to protect our democracy. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu recalled that legislators continued to defend democratic principles despite the dissolution of the National Assembly during military rule. * We were jailed for our defiance. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Recalling the events following the dissolution of the National Assembly in 1993, Tinubu referred to his participation with other pro-democracy figures who reconvened in defiance of the military government and were subsequently imprisoned. * On behalf of a grateful nation, I commend your invaluable role in lawmaking, oversight, and constituency representation. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu expressed the nation's appreciation to members of the National Assembly for their constitutional responsibilities in legislation, oversight, and representation. * At this point, I plead for your indulgence so that I may put a terrible rumour to bed. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu introduced a section of his address in which he responded to public speculation about the future of Nigeria's multi-party democratic system. * To those who ring the alarm that the APC is intent on a one-party state, I offer you a most personal promise. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu addressed concerns that the ruling party sought to establish a one-party state, introducing his personal assurance on the matter. * At no time in the past, nor any instance in the present, and at no future juncture shall I view the notion of a one-party state as good for Nigeria. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu stated that he does not support the idea of Nigeria becoming a one-party state, reaffirming his position during the Democracy Day address. * I have never attempted to alter any political party registration with INEC. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu rejected allegations that he had sought to interfere with the registration of political parties by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). * Look at my political history. I would be the last person to advocate such a scheme. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Responding to claims that his administration intended to establish a one-party state, President Tinubu cited his own political history as evidence of his commitment to multiparty democracy. * In 2003, when the then-governing party tried to sweep the nation clean of political opposition through plot and manipulation, I was the last of the progressive governors standing in my region. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu recalled his experience as Governor of Lagos State during the 2003 elections, describing how he remained the only progressive governor in his region after other opposition states were lost. * Yet, I stood alone. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Reflecting on the 2003 political landscape, Tinubu emphasized that he remained the sole progressive governor in his geopolitical zone despite intense political pressure. * Nigeria will not become such a state now. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.After recounting his opposition to attempts at political domination in 2003, President Tinubu reaffirmed that Nigeria would not become a one-party state under his leadership. * A one-party state is not in the offing. Nor should it ever be. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu made an unequivocal statement rejecting the idea of a one-party state and reaffirming his support for Nigeria's multiparty democracy. * Equally, my friends, we cannot blame anybody seeking to bail out of a sinking ship even without a life jacket. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.While responding to criticisms over opposition politicians joining the APC, President Tinubu argued that individuals cannot be faulted for leaving political parties they believe are failing. * In all their numbers and false grandeur, they boasted of ruling, not governing, Nigeria for the next half century or more. Where are they now? ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu recalled the political dominance claimed by the then-ruling party in the early 2000s, arguing that political power is ultimately temporary. * My allies had been induced into defeat. My adversaries held all the cards that mortal man could carry. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Reflecting on the 2003 political environment, Tinubu described the overwhelming political advantage enjoyed by his opponents and the setbacks suffered by his allies. * Even with all of that, they could not control our national destiny because fate is written from above. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu attributed Nigeria's democratic trajectory to divine providence rather than political calculation or human power. * A greater power did not want Nigeria to become a one-party state back then. Nigeria will not become such a state now. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.Tinubu argued that Nigeria's continued multiparty democracy reflects both the country's political resilience and divine providence, reaffirming his opposition to a one-party state. * We must welcome and accept the diversity and number of political parties just as we welcome and embrace the diversity of our population. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu reaffirmed his support for Nigeria's multiparty democratic system, arguing that political diversity is as important as the country's social and ethnic diversity. * Our efforts must never be to eliminate political competition but to make that competition salutary to the national well-being by working across the political aisle whenever possible. ** https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-speech-at-the-national-assembly-in-commemoration-of-democracy-day/.President Tinubu argued that Nigeria's multiparty democracy should encourage healthy political competition and cooperation across party lines for the benefit of the nation. == External links == {{wikipedia}} {{commons}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tinubu, Bola}} [[Category:Presidents of Nigeria]] [[Category:Muslims]] [[Category:1952 births]] [[Category:Living people]]

[[File:Edgars Rinkēvičs as president-elect, 2023-05-31 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Edgars Rinkēvičs in 2023]] '''{{w|Edgars Rinkēvičs}}''' (born 21 September 1973) is a [[Latvia]]n public official and politician serving as the 11th and current [[w:president of Latvia|president of Latvia]] since July 2023. He previously served as the [[w:Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Latvia)|minister of foreign affairs of Latvia]] from 2011 to 2023, and head of the [[w:President of Latvia|Chancery of the President of Latvia]] as state secretary of the [[w:Ministry of Defence (Latvia)|Ministry of Defence]], as well as a deputy of the [[w:Saeima|Saeima]]. Upon taking office as president, Rinkēvičs became the first openly gay [[w:head of state|head of state]] in a [[European Union]] country. Prior to becoming president, Rinkēvičs had represented [[w:Latvian Way|Latvian Way]], [[w:Reform Party (Latvia)|Reform Party]], and the [[w:Unity (Latvia)|Unity]] party since May 2014. He left Unity after being elected president as it is customarily expected in Latvia for presidents to maintain political neutrality. ==Quotes== * A year ago Russia started full scale war against Ukraine, many doubted if Ukrainians would withstand. They did, their moral victory is great.
Today many ask, if Ukraine can win militarily. The answer is yes and we must send more weapons, more help.
Ruzzia delenda est ** [https://x.com/edgarsrinkevics/status/1629091864031727617 24 February 2023] on Twitter ** Alluding to [[w:Carthago delenda est|''Carthago delenda est'']] by [[Cato the Elder]] * I fully support @EmmanuelMacron: we should not draw red lines for ourselves, we must draw red lines for Russia and we should not be afraid to enforce them. Ukraine must win, Russia must be defeated. Russia delenda est! ** [https://x.com/edgarsrinkevics/status/1768533827897397433 March 15 2024] on Twitter ==External links== * {{wikipedia-inline}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Rinkēvičs, Edgars}} [[Category:1973 births]] [[Category:Politicians from Latvia]] [[Category:Foreign ministers]] [[Category:Defense ministers]] [[Category:LGBT people]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Heads of state]]

Q195725.wikitext:
[[File:President Ruto Potrait 2022 (cropped).jpg|thumb]]
'''[[w:William Ruto|William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto CGH]]''' (born 21 December 1966) is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current [[w:President of Kenya|President of Kenya]] since 13 September 2022. Prior to becoming president, he served as the first elected [[w:Deputy President of Kenya|Deputy President of Kenya]] from 2013 to 2022.

== Quotes ==
*The greatest con job ever perpetrated by saying that science and facts are very stubborn.
*Climate change is real.
*Climate action is absolutely necessary.
*You cannot reverse the trends that are going on. Floods are ravaging continents, wildfires, drought and everything in between.
*There is only a resolution through dialogue.
**[https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/t%C3%AAte-%C3%A0-t%C3%AAte/20250925-unless-the-un-is-reformed-its-own-survival-is-at-stake-kenya-s-ruto-says 'Unless the UN is reformed, its own survival is at stake,' Kenya's Ruto says]; ''Retrieved on 25/09/2025''

*I think AGOA is working pretty well, even in its current form. For example, last year, Kenya exported $544 million — close to 70 to 80 billion [Kenyan shillings] worth of goods to the United States — quota free, duty free. I think last year, we added 12,000 jobs under this program. ... We're making huge progress in making sure that Kenyan products can have access to American markets the same way we have negotiated the Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Union to facilitate trade and access to market for goods from Kenya.
*The court asked us to have an agreement signed between Kenya and Haiti specifically to facilitate this deployment. The prime minister of Haiti [Ariel Henry] traveled to Kenya, and we jintly witnessed the signing of that agreement.
*"The deployment of our security officers to Haiti has been endorsed by the Cabinet. Both houses of parliament have ratified it. We have met all international requirements, and in fact, we have complied with the very court order you're referring to.
**[https://www.voanews.com/a/ruto-declares-ironclad-support-for-haiti-in-exclusive-interview-/7630550.html Ruto declares ironclad support for Haiti in exclusive interview];''By Hubbah Abdi,Retrieved on May 28, 2024''

Q5937916.title: José Antonio Kast
Q5937916.wikitext:
[[File:Retrato Presidente José Antonio Kast.png|thumb|Official portrait (2026).]]
'''[[w:José Antonio Kast|José Antonio Kast]]''' (born 18 January 1966) is a Chilean politician who has served as President of Chile since 2026. He previously served as a member of the Chamber of Deputies and founded the Republican Party of Chile.

==Quotes==
===As Candidate: 2017–2025===
====2017====
* ''Si Pinochet estuviera vivo, votaría por mí.''
** Translation: "If Pinochet were alive, he would vote for me."
** José Antonio Kast, discussing former Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet, in [https://www.t13.cl/radio/politica/mesa-central/noticia/kast-si-pinochet-estuviera-vivo-votaria-por-mi "Kast: 'Si Pinochet estuviera vivo, votaría por mí'"], ''T13'' (November 9, 2017).

* ''Conozco a Miguel Krassnoff y viéndolo no creo todas las cosas que se dicen de él.''
** Translation: "I know Miguel Krassnoff, and having met him, I don't believe everything that is said about him."
** José Antonio Kast, discussing former military officer Miguel Krassnoff, convicted of crimes against humanity, in [https://www.elmostrador.cl/noticias/pais/2017/11/09/jose-antonio-kast-conozco-a-miguel-krassnoff-y-viendolo-no-creo-todas-las-cosas-que-se-dicen-de-el/ "José Antonio Kast: «Conozco a Miguel Krassnoff y viéndolo no creo todas las cosas que se dicen de él»"], ''El Mostrador'' (November 9, 2017).

* ''No creo en el matrimonio igualitario, porque creo que dos hombres no son igual que un hombre y una mujer. Dos hombres no pueden procrear.''
** Translation: "I don't believe in same-sex marriage, because I believe that two men are not the same as a man and a woman. Two men cannot procreate."
** José Antonio Kast, in [https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/nacional/chile/2017/07/17/jose-antonio-kast-no-creo-en-el-matrimonio-igualitario.shtml "José Antonio Kast: 'No creo en el matrimonio igualitario'"], ''BioBioChile'' (July 17, 2017).

====2021====
* ''Nunca voy a ser partidario del aborto, en ninguna instancia. Soy defensor de la vida.''
** Translation: "I will never support abortion under any circumstances. I defend life."
** José Antonio Kast, discussing abortion legislation during his presidential campaign, in [https://www.24horas.cl/politica/kast-reitera-rechazo-al-matrimonio-igualitario-es-entre-un-hombre-y-una-mujer-5072816 "Kast reitera rechazo al matrimonio igualitario: 'Es entre un hombre y una mujer'"], ''24 Horas'' (November 23, 2021).

====2025====
* ''Les quedan 128 días a los inmigrantes irregulares para dejar el país.''
** Translation: "Undocumented immigrants have 128 days left to leave the country."
** José Antonio Kast, discussing his proposed immigration policy during a presidential debate, in [https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2025/11/04/1182257/frases-candidatos-presidenciales-debate-archi.html "Migración, violencia en liceos y Punta Peuco: Las 12 frases de los candidatos que marcaron el debate"], ''Emol'' (November 4, 2025).

===President of Chile: 2026–2030===
* ''No ganamos esta elección para vivir en un palacio ni para ocupar un cargo, ganamos esta elección para trabajar por los chilenos, para los chilenos.''
** Translation: "We didn't win this election to live in a palace or to hold office; we won this election to work for Chileans, for Chileans."
** José Antonio Kast, in his first presidential address from La Moneda, [https://prensa.presidencia.cl/discurso.aspx?id=322223 "S.E. el Presidente de la República, José Antonio Kast, se dirige por primera vez al país desde el Palacio de La Moneda"], ''Presidencia de la República de Chile'' (March 11, 2026).

* ''El mensaje es claro y directo: los chilenos van a recuperar su libertad, y los delincuentes y narcotraficantes la perderán para siempre. Por primera vez, el Estado va a decir en su propia Constitución que proteger a su gente no es una opción más, sino una obligación.''
** Translation: "The message is clear and direct: Chileans will regain their freedom, and criminals and drug traffickers will lose theirs forever. For the first time, the State will declare in its own Constitution that protecting its people is not merely an option, but an obligation."
** José Antonio Kast, presenting his government's security agenda, quoted in [https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2026/08/06/1207719/frases-cadena-nacional-kast.html "'Los chilenos van a recuperar su libertad' y 'habrá algunos que querrán oponerse': Las 10 frases del discurso de Kast"], ''Emol'' (August 6, 2026).

* ''No vamos a quitar ningún derecho adquirido, sino que a trabajar en base a las normas establecidas en materia laboral.''
** Translation: "We are not going to take away any acquired rights, but rather work within the established labor regulations."
** José Antonio Kast, discussing labor policy in an interview with [https://cooperativa.cl/noticias/pais/presidente-kast/presidente-jose-antonio-kast-no-vamos-a-retirar-la-reforma/2026-08-31/070722.html "Presidente José Antonio Kast: Si las críticas son a causa de prejuicios, quienes las emiten son opinólogos"], ''Cooperativa'' (August 31, 2026).

Q4414390.title: Li Qiang
Q4414390.wikitext:
[[File:Li_Qiang_(20230313).jpg|thumb|In particular, we will enhance our capacity for scientific and technological innovation, build a modern industrial system, and transition toward green development.]]
[[File:"Shanghai Thank You" on a building of Shanghai.jpg|thumb|Talking about difficulties, I think all countries are confronted with some difficulties, and we see no less difficulty for China this year.]]
'''[[w:Li Qiang|Li Qiang]]''' ('''Chinese''':李强) (born [[23 July]] [[1959]]) is a Chinese politician, currently serving as the 8th [[w:Premier of the People's Republic of China|premier of the State Council of China]] since March 2023. He has served as the second-ranking member on the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP) [[w:Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|Central Committee]] [[w:Politburo Standing Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|Politburo Standing Committee]] since October 2022. He previously served as [[w:Chinese Communist Party Committee Secretary|party secretary]] of [[Shanghai|Shanghai City]] from 2017 to 2022, party secretary of [[w:Jiangsu|Jiangsu Province]] from 2016 to 2017, and [[governor]] of [[w:Zhejiang|Zhejiang Province]] from 2012 to 2016.

==Quotes==
<small>[https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng/zxxx_662805/202303/t20230314_11040394.html "Premier Li Qiang Meets the Press: Full Transcript of Questions and Answers"] (13 March 2023)</small>
*We will firmly follow a people-centered development approach. The ultimate aim of the work of the Party and the government is to improve the well-being of the people. As General Secretary [[Xi Jinping]] pointed out, people’s aspiration for a better life is our goal. We will always bear in mind that ours is a people’s government, and we will make solid efforts on every piece of work concerning people’s livelihood.

*Honestly speaking, most people do not keep their eyes on GDP growth all the time. What they care more about are the things that happen in their everyday life, like housing, employment, income, education, medical services and the environment. Therefore, the government must always plan and carry out its work according to the people’s wish.

*Currently, our development is focused on providing for people’s basic needs. Going forward, the focus will be shifted toward delivering a life of better quality for the people. In particular, we will enhance our capacity for scientific and technological innovation, build a modern industrial system, and transition toward green development.

*All in all, we will make greater efforts to fully and faithfully apply the new development philosophy on all fronts, move faster to create a new development paradigm and concentrate on promoting high-quality development.

*As for our specific work going forward, we will introduce a number of policy combinations as follows: a combination of macro policies, a combination of policies for expanding demand, a combination of policies for advancing reform and innovation, and a combination of policies for preventing and defusing risks. These policy combinations will all be supported by concrete implementing steps. We will enrich, adjust and improve these policy combinations in the course of implementation. 

*Talking about difficulties, I think all countries are confronted with some difficulties, and we see no less difficulty for China this year. But think about it. Is there any single period or any single year where we had no difficulty at all? The Chinese people have always pulled through difficult times and achieved new progress.

*Economic development follows certain economic laws and depends on the conditions available. However, it is even more important to bring out people’s initiative. So I do hope that private entrepreneurs will carry forward the entrepreneurial spirit and strengthen confidence as they start their new journey. 

* I’m happy to answer questions raised by the netizens. When I have time, I also go online quite a lot to see what the netizens are thinking and what suggestions they have for the work of the government. 

*Employment is the cornerstone of people’s livelihood. Ultimately, the solution to job creation lies in economic growth. As for the specific steps going forward, we will continue to pursue the employment-first strategy. We will increase government support in terms of employment services and technical training. We will take multiple steps to stabilize and expand employment. We will support and regulate the development of new forms of employment. 

*When assessing demographic dividend, we should look at not just the quantity but also the quality of population. We should not just look at the sheer size of the population, but also look at the scale of high-caliber workforce. 

*China is a country with a large population and unbalanced development. Yet it only took us less than two months to achieve a smooth transition in COVID response phase and normal economic and social order was restored in a relatively short span of time. This is indeed a remarkable achievement. What has happened proves that China’s COVID strategies and measures are completely right and our COVID response has been highly effective. 

*Chinese on both sides of the Taiwan Strait are members of one and the same family. We share an unbreakable bond of blood and kinship. We will continue to promote economic and cultural exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait on the basis of the [[w:One-China policy|one-China principle]] and the [[w:1992 Consensus|1992 Consensus]]. We also encourage more Taiwan compatriots and businesses to come to the mainland. We hope they will not just be willing to come to the mainland, but also be able to integrate into the local communities and achieve better development.

*Rural revitalization is not just about economic growth. In my view, it is also important to fully bring out the economic, ecological, social and cultural value of the countryside. 

*The new mission and new task have raised new and higher requirements on us. We will take the new round of state institutional reform as an opportunity to strengthen government-building. We will further transform government functions, make the government’s work more efficient and improve the conduct of the government.

Q527020.title: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
Q527020.wikitext:
'''[[w:Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah|Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah]]''' (born 29 October 1952) is a [[Namibia]]n politician who is Namibia's fifth president as of 2025. She previously served as the third vice president and as the [[w:Deputy-Prime Minister of Namibia|deputy prime minister of Namibia]] from 2015 to 2024. Previously the [[w:SWAPO|SWAPO]] vice president, she became the party's first female presidential candidate in November 2024. She has also served as Namibia's [[w:List of Ministers of Foreign Affairs of Namibia|Minister of International Relations and Cooperation]] since December 2012. From March 2010 to December 2012, she was [[w:Ministry of Environment and Tourism (Namibia)|Minister of Environment and Tourism]]. Nandi-Ndaitwah is a member of SWAPO, Namibia's ruling party, and a long-time member of the [[w:National Assembly of Namibia|National Assembly]]. In 2017, Nandi-Ndaitwah was elected [[w:Vice president|vice-president]] of the Swapo Party at the party's 6th Congress. She is the first woman to serve in that position.

==Quotes==
*We are too few to be poor and we can eradicate poverty.[https://www.parliament.na/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/2025_State_of_the_Nation_Address_by_H_E_Dr_Netumbo_Nandi_Ndaitwah.pdf]

**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid0c7gLePeEvToLvNLqPcb5RByeshL9sAaCXqSqS2YxMYz8jUwFDZGSyW2cCEKKAAq1l/?app=fbl]
*You will not reach your destination when you don't know where you are going, you must have fixed thoughts for you to reach your goals. With Netumbo as your vise president targets will be time framed for evaluation into better path,we will raise and fly together. 
**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid02RxAPfdxqqJY7pQESpyZpJbVLnvwxkeK53U7SXrrthwWt82jdQUzpKPwq9HJxQSCYl/?app=fbl]
*In order for you to move forward you need to be surrounded by people with vision not with emotions, you need the by side with solutions not with issues. With Netumbo as your vise president you will have vision and solutions by your side to enable you  move forward in life.
**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid0kJrQfS8k6jKwTLH4VYrH9C6BKzEX3TmsZyWeheCtEzgNhHsrMuMyGpgQWN5Hd2wDl/?app=fbl]
*A caterpillar is a slow walker but it keeps moving until it finds a right season that helps it turns into a butterfly. Even you no matter what you are going through don't quit joy is coming,change places, do things over and over again until you find a right season that will make you hetch into a butterfly and fly better.
**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid0325GVR9dXuQvv7y4iJrtf7AgQerUCtwbAy8yNvCqvpxs3Am1w4XpJuExazJecnVCcl/?app=fbl]
*Don't allow the pressure of those eating their harvest make you eat your seed.
**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid02tSCipAJyMHiQfPDQJeaiQRePojXKjffVsok5igB2bTrfF8scbvpwqhy5oj1ZCYzgl/?app=fbl]
*When a soldier enters war his priority is not to survive but to assassinate the enemy and he automatically survives. Our target must not be to survive but to encounter poverty and we will be automatically successful.
**[https://www.facebook.com/292678045858286/posts/pfbid0oETNiwbe2257FvjvjyX1X49hizMDGcVVVp71HPPq9tnMmqyRgwdTPbWtJ7qczjWEl/?app=fbl]
* USA is the oldest democracy in the world but they only have two political parties
**[https://www.observer24.com.na/tag/deputy-prime-minister-netumbo-nandi-ndaitwah/]

* The election manifesto prioritizes social development and empowerment for all Namibians. This is why Namibians should vote for SWAPO.

* The party has committed to creating approximately 256,000 jobs over the course of her five-year term.

* These commitments encompass the development of sports infrastructure, career advancement, education, as well as the arts and creative industries.

* To ensure the full implementation of this manifesto by 2030, an action plan will be developed, aligned with a monitoring and evaluation framework.

* There are external forces attempting to destabilize us, but as a nation, the future is in our hands, and unity is the only tool we have to overcome these challenges.
** [https://www.observer24.com.na/swapo-promises-n85-billion-for-job-creation/]
** Former diplomatic representative of Namibia, Ambassador Pius Dunaiski said such empty promises have been made since independence, and Swapo has failed dismally.

**[https://www.namibian.com.na/president-says-corruption-must-be-compared-to-treason/ President says corruption must be compared to treason] namibian.com.na (21 March 2026)
*“When resources meant to improve the lives of our people are misused, it becomes an injustice to every Namibian who depends on those resources for better schools, healthcare, housing and opportunities,”
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/president-says-corruption-must-be-compared-to-treason/ President says corruption must be compared to treason] namibian.com.na (21 March 2026)
*“It is saddening to see these elements increasingly showing their ‘ugly face’ in our nation. They are dangerous, they tear nations apart and must be avoided at all costs,”
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/president-says-corruption-must-be-compared-to-treason/ President says corruption must be compared to treason] namibian.com.na (21 March 2026)
*“The eighth administration is determined to advance national priorities, with agriculture remaining priority number one,” 
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/president-says-corruption-must-be-compared-to-treason/ President says corruption must be compared to treason] namibian.com.na (21 March 2026)
*“Climate change is placing increasing pressure on land and water resources,”
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/nandi-ndaitwah-and-johnson-sirleaf-lead-talks-on-african-women-leadership/ Nandi-Ndaitwah and Johnson Sirleaf lead talks on African women leadership] namibian.com.na(4 February 20214 February 2026)
*“We must, therefore, translate political commitment into valuable projects and tangible results,”
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/nandi-ndaitwah-calls-for-more-investment-in-water/ Nandi-Ndaitwah calls for more investment in water] namibian.com.na(22 September 2026)
**The target is to make an additional US$30 billion available annually by 2030. Nandi-Ndaitwah said Namibia is ready to attract investment into water infrastructure, including purification, aquifer recharge, raw-water distribution and desalination under the Sixth National Development Plan.
*“Young people should be regarded as partners in shaping the future rather than merely beneficiaries,” 
**[https://www.namibian.com.na/pact-must-deliver-for-africa-nandi-ndaitwah/ Pact must deliver for Africa – Nandi-Ndaitwah]  namibian.com.na (23 September 2026)
**She highlighted financing for development as another key priority, including reforms to the international financial architecture, technology transfer and international tax cooperation
**“Young people should be regarded as partners in shaping the future rather than merely beneficiaries,” she said. She urged member states to bring implementation of the pact home, saying its real test would be its national uptake and the impact delivered at country level..
**Speaking at a high-level side event on the implementation of the Pact for the Future in Africa on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, Nandi-Ndaitwah said Africa had taken ownership of the pact’s implementation.

* I am well pleased, that thanks to our (Mongolia–Azerbaijan) joint efforts the mutually beneficial bilateral cooperation is strengthening in many areas. Furthermore, I am confident that the bilateral cooperation will be enriched with economic content by expanding in the fields of agriculture, transportation and tourism.
** Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh (2023) cited in: "[https://www.azernews.az/nation/210789.html President of Mongolia sends letter to President Ilham Aliyev on occasion of May 28 - Independence Day]" in ''Azernews'', 6 June 2023.

* Mongolia has actively supported and collaborated on initiatives proposed by [[United Nations]] member states to advance [[sustainable development]] in mountainous regions, combat climate change and enhance adaptation and resilience.
** Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh (2024) cited in: "[https://montsame.mn/en/read/355807 Khurelsukh Ukhnaa: Mongolia is Keen to Preserve the Balance of the Mountain Ecosystem]" in ''Mongolian National News Agency'', 13 November 2024.

* With a profound awareness of our duty to safeguard the sacred hearth of the Great Mongol Empire established by [[Genghis Khan]], let us cherish and honor the values of statehood, preserve and pass on our precious cultural heritage and history to future generations, promote harmony, uphold righteousness, observe proper conduct, and work together to advance and develop Mongolia.
** Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh (2024) cited in: "[https://montsame.mn/en/read/358662 President Khurelsukh Extends New Year Greetings]" in ''Mongolian National News Agency'', 31 December 2024.

* We need to urgently establish a comprehensive and modernized [[cancer]] treatment and research facility that meets international standards.  With Mongolia's expanding foreign relations, we intend to advance this project through international cooperation and not rely solely on the State Budget. Cancer incidence is increasing each year, and without the timely completion of this facility, the [[World Health Organization]] estimates that cancer rates in Mongolia will double by 2040.
** Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh (2025) cited in: "[https://montsame.mn/en/read/359021 The Second National Oncology Center to Be Commissioned in 2030]" in ''Mongolian National News Agency'', 6 January 2025.

* You (Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat) had dedicated your entire life to the service to your country (Mongolia), from an ordinary herder to the president of the country, from a mining engineer to a minister, scientist and academician.
** Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh (2025) cited in: "[https://montsame.mn/en/read/360438 Mongolia Bids Farewell to Honorable Ochirbat Punsalmaa]" in ''Mongolian National News Agency'', 24 January 2025.
